{{Short description|Football award}} {{Use dmy dates|date=January 2023}} {{Infobox award | name = 2007 Ballon d'Or | subheader = | image = Kaka06052007.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = 2007 Ballon d'Or winner, [[Kaká]] | awarded_for = | date = {{start date|2007|12|02|df=y}} | location = [[Paris]], France | country = France | presenter = ''[[France Football]]'' | host = | former name = | preshow_host = | acts = | website = {{URL|ballondor.com}} | runtime = | award1_type = Won by | award1_winner= {{flagicon|BRA}} [[Kaká]] (1st award) | previous = [[2006 Ballon d'Or|2006]] | main = [[Ballon d'Or]] | next = [[2008 Ballon d'Or|2008]] }} The '''2007 Ballon d'Or''' ({{lit|'''2007 Golden Ball'''}}), given to the best [[Association football|football]] player in the world given out by [[France Football]] and [[UEFA]] and judged by an international panel of sports journalists, was awarded to [[Kaká]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/europa-poy07.html |title=European Footballer of the Year ("Ballon d'Or") 2007 |publisher=[[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|RSSSF]] |date=9 October 2008| access-date = 5 December 2008| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20081024172719/http://www.rsssf.com/miscellaneous/europa-poy07.html| archive-date= 24 October 2008 | url-status= live}}{{Cite web |url=http://francefootball.fr/FF/breves2007/20071202_105047Dev.html |title=Kakà, King of the World |publisher=[[France Football]] |date=2 December 2007| access-date= 5 December 2008| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20081217021622/http://www.francefootball.fr/FF/breves2007/20071202_105047Dev.html| archive-date= 17 December 2008| url-status= dead}} This was the first year in which players from clubs outside the [[UEFA]] federation were eligible for nomination; this change also led to an increase in the voting pool to include journalists from outside UEFA countries.{{Cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/7750910.stm |title=Kaka wins 2007 award |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=1 December 2008| access-date = 5 December 2008| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20081204115634/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/7750910.stm| archive-date= 4 December 2008 | url-status= live}} Kaká was the fourth Brazilian national to win the award after [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]] ([[1997 Ballon d'Or|1997]], [[2002 Ballon d'Or|2002]]), [[Rivaldo]] ([[1999 Ballon d'Or|1999]]), and [[Ronaldinho]] ([[2005 Ballon d'Or|2005]]). He was the sixth [[AC Milan]] player to win the trophy after [[Gianni Rivera]] ([[1969 Ballon d'Or|1969]]), [[Ruud Gullit]] ([[1987 Ballon d'Or|1987]]), [[Marco van Basten]] ([[1988 Ballon d'Or|1988]], [[1989 Ballon d'Or|1989]], [[1992 Ballon d'Or|1992]]), [[George Weah]] ([[1995 Ballon d'Or|1995]]), and [[Andriy Shevchenko]] ([[2004 Ballon d'Or|2004]]). The ceremony is notable as Kaká was the last player to win the [[Ballon d'Or]] before the [[Messi–Ronaldo rivalry|Messi–Ronaldo]] dominance of the award.
